There is **no link between the MMR vaccine and autism**. This is the consensus of every major medical and scientific organization worldwide:

- The original 1998 study suggesting a link was **retracted** and proven to be **fraudulent** (Andrew Wakefield lost his medical license)
- Numerous large-scale studies involving millions of children have found **no association** between MMR vaccination and autism spectrum disorder
- Major organizations including the **WHO**, **CDC**, ** AMA**, and **National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine** all affirm no causal link exists

The concern originated from a fraudulent study that has been thoroughly debunked. The MMR vaccine remains one of the safest and most important public health interventions, and it is not responsible for the rise in autism diagnoses (which researchers attribute to broader diagnostic criteria and increased awareness).
